newsitem.title: USA: NH Democrat Shaheen must contend with Republicans.
newsitem.headline: NH Democrat Shaheen must contend with Republicans.

text.p: Democrats made inroads in the traditional Republican stronghold of New Hampshire, but saw initial projections of an almost historic victory sweep fall painfully short.

New Hampshire voters Tuesday supported President Clinton just as they did in 1992. It marked the first time in 96 years that Democrats have won back-to-back presidential contests in the conservative state.

Democrat Jeanne Shaheen, 49, became the first woman ever elected New Hampshire's governor, defeating Republican Ovide Lamontagne. The state has gubernatorial elections every two years and Democrats last won the office in 1980.

Shaheen, a state legislator from Madbury, will replace Gov. Stephen Merrill, a popular Republican who surprised the state's political observers earlier this year when he decided not to seek re-election.

"I'm sure we can work with her. Afterall, I've worked with her in the Senate," said Sen. Richard Danais while having lunch at the Merrimack River restaurant in Manchester, N.H. where they serve up politics along with apple pie. "The question is really can she work with us. We still control the Legislature."
Democrats thought they had ousted an incumbent Republican senator in 64 years. But media exit poll projections that showed former Rep Dick Swett beating Sen. Bob Smith turned out to be inacurate.

Republicans also won two tight House races. Freshman Rep. Charles Bass fought off a challenge by Deborah Arnesen, while John E. Sununu - son of the former White House chief of staff and New Hampshire governor - defeated former Democratic Party chairman Joe Keefe. It was Keefe's third bid for the office.
